title: Quran, Sura 44 (ad-duḫān) (Codex Parisino-petropolitanus)
source: Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328) via Gallica IIIF + Corpus Coranicum folio mapping + Tanzil + Pickthall
description: Sura 44 (ad-duḫān) from the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (c. 650-750 AD), one section per folio side, each linked to the exact Gallica image of that page (3 pages).
introduction:
Sura 44 (ad-duḫān) as preserved on 3 folio sides of the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (Paris, BnF Arabe 328 (a) and (b)), one of the oldest surviving Quran manuscripts, written in hijazi script on parchment, c. 650-750 AD. Each section below is one folio side, and the image shown is that exact page.

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side from Gallica (Bibliotheque nationale de France IIIF). The folio's sura:verse range was taken from the Corpus Coranicum "Manuscripta Coranica" record for that page, which states the first and last word on the page; the folio numbers of both services were cross-checked by comparing the two images pixel by pixel.
  2. Original text: the Arabic of the Tanzil Project Uthmani text (CC BY 3.0), reproduced unchanged, verse by verse.
  3. English: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain, verse by verse.

Orthography: the codex is written in scriptio defectiva: no vowel signs, almost no consonantal dots, long vowels often unwritten, and letter shapes that differ from the printed Uthmani text. The modern text given here therefore differs orthographically from what is on the folio while conveying the same reading; readers should expect, for example, the basmala and words such as qala to be spelled with fewer letters on the page.

Numbering: verse numbers follow the standard Kufan (Cairo 1924) division used by Corpus Coranicum, Tanzil and Pickthall. Early codices mark verse ends with ink dots that in places divide the text differently, so a verse count made on the page may not match these numbers exactly. In Tanzil's text the basmala opening each sura (except sura 9) is printed as part of verse 1. Where a page begins or ends in the middle of a verse the whole verse is given and the word position is stated in the section heading.
translator_notes: All 59 verses of this sura are present on the Paris leaves (3 folio sides).
Corpus Coranicum records the first and last word of each page; a verse split across two pages is shown in full under both pages with the word position noted.

translation.original_ref: Quran 44:1-12, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 62r (page ends at word 6 of 44:12; page begins in sura 43 (43:78))
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ حمٓ <sup>2</sup>وَٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ <sup>3</sup>إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ <sup>4</sup>فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ <sup>5</sup>أَمْرًا مِّنْ عِندِنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ <sup>6</sup>رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ <sup>7</sup>رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ <sup>8</sup>لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ <sup>9</sup>بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ <sup>10</sup>فَٱرْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِى ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِينٍ <sup>11</sup>يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ <sup>12</sup>رَّبَّنَا ٱكْشِفْ عَنَّا ٱلْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Ha. Mim. <sup>2</sup>By the Scripture that maketh plain <sup>3</sup>Lo! We revealed it on a blessed night - Lo! We are ever warning - <sup>4</sup>Whereon every wise command is made clear <sup>5</sup>As a command from Our presence - Lo! We are ever sending - <sup>6</sup>A mercy from thy Lord. Lo! He, even He is the Hearer, the Knower, <sup>7</sup>Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye would be sure. <sup>8</sup>There is no Allah save Him. He quickeneth and giveth death; your Lord and Lord of your forefathers. <sup>9</sup>Nay, but they play in doubt. <sup>10</sup>But watch thou (O Muhammad) for the day when the sky will produce visible smoke <sup>11</sup>That will envelop the people. This will be a painful torment. <sup>12</sup>(Then they will say): Our Lord relieve us of the torment. Lo! we are believers.

translation.original_ref: Quran 44:13-39, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 62v (page ends at word 8 of 44:39)
translation.original_text: <sup>13</sup>أَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ وَقَدْ جَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُّبِينٌ <sup>14</sup>ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا۟ عَنْهُ وَقَالُوا۟ مُعَلَّمٌ مَّجْنُونٌ <sup>15</sup>إِنَّا كَاشِفُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ <sup>16</sup>يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰٓ إِنَّا مُنتَقِمُونَ <sup>17</sup>وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ <sup>18</sup>أَنْ أَدُّوٓا۟ إِلَىَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ <sup>19</sup>وَأَن لَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم بِسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ <sup>20</sup>وَإِنِّى عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُمْ أَن تَرْجُمُونِ <sup>21</sup>وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُوا۟ لِى فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ <sup>22</sup>فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوْمٌ مُّجْرِمُونَ <sup>23</sup>فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى لَيْلًا إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ <sup>24</sup>وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا إِنَّهُمْ جُندٌ مُّغْرَقُونَ <sup>25</sup>كَمْ تَرَكُوا۟ مِن جَنَّٰتٍ وَعُيُونٍ <sup>26</sup>وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ <sup>27</sup>وَنَعْمَةٍ كَانُوا۟ فِيهَا فَٰكِهِينَ <sup>28</sup>كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَٰهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ <sup>29</sup>فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُنظَرِينَ <sup>30</sup>وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ <sup>31</sup>مِن فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَالِيًا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ <sup>32</sup>وَلَقَدِ ٱخْتَرْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ <sup>33</sup>وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلَٰٓؤٌا۟ مُّبِينٌ <sup>34</sup>إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ لَيَقُولُونَ <sup>35</sup>إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُنشَرِينَ <sup>36</sup>فَأْتُوا۟ بِـَٔابَآئِنَآ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ <sup>37</sup>أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ مُجْرِمِينَ <sup>38</sup>وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ <sup>39</sup>مَا خَلَقْنَٰهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
translation.text: <sup>13</sup>How can there be remembrance for them, when a messenger making plain (the Truth) had already come unto them, <sup>14</sup>And they had turned away from him and said: One taught (by others), a madman? <sup>15</sup>Lo! We withdraw the torment a little. Lo! ye return (to disbelief). <sup>16</sup>On the day when We shall seize them with the greater seizure, (then) in truth We shall punish. <sup>17</sup>And verily We tried before them Pharaoh's folk, when there came unto them a noble messenger, <sup>18</sup>Saying: Give up to me the slaves of Allah. Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you. <sup>19</sup>And saying: Be not proud against Allah. Lo! I bring you a clear warrant. <sup>20</sup>And lo! I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest ye stone me to death. <sup>21</sup>And if ye put no faith in me, then let me go. <sup>22</sup>And he cried unto his Lord, (saying): These are guilty folk. <sup>23</sup>Then (his Lord commanded): Take away My slaves by night. Lo! ye will be followed, <sup>24</sup>And leave the sea behind at rest, for lo! they are a drowned host. <sup>25</sup>How many were the gardens and the watersprings that they left behind, <sup>26</sup>And the cornlands and the goodly sites <sup>27</sup>And pleasant things wherein they took delight! <sup>28</sup>Even so (it was), and We made it an inheritance for other folk; <sup>29</sup>And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved. <sup>30</sup>And We delivered the Children of Israel from the shameful doom; <sup>31</sup>(We delivered them) from Pharaoh. Lo! he was a tyrant of the wanton ones. <sup>32</sup>And We chose them, purposely, above (all) creatures. <sup>33</sup>And We gave them portents wherein was a clear trial. <sup>34</sup>Lo! these, forsooth, are saying: <sup>35</sup>There is naught but our first death, and we shall not be raised again. <sup>36</sup>Bring back our fathers, if ye speak the truth! <sup>37</sup>Are they better, or the folk of Tubb'a and those before them? We destroyed them, for surely they were guilty. <sup>38</sup>And We created not the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in play. <sup>39</sup>We created them not save with truth; but most of them know not.

translation.original_ref: Quran 44:40-59, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 63r (page continues into sura 45 (45:7))
translation.original_text: <sup>40</sup>إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ مِيقَٰتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ <sup>41</sup>يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِى مَوْلًى عَن مَّوْلًى شَيْـًٔا وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ <sup>42</sup>إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ <sup>43</sup>إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ ٱلزَّقُّومِ <sup>44</sup>طَعَامُ ٱلْأَثِيمِ <sup>45</sup>كَٱلْمُهْلِ يَغْلِى فِى ٱلْبُطُونِ <sup>46</sup>كَغَلْىِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ <sup>47</sup>خُذُوهُ فَٱعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ <sup>48</sup>ثُمَّ صُبُّوا۟ فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِۦ مِنْ عَذَابِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ <sup>49</sup>ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ <sup>50</sup>إِنَّ هَٰذَا مَا كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَمْتَرُونَ <sup>51</sup>إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ <sup>52</sup>فِى جَنَّٰتٍ وَعُيُونٍ <sup>53</sup>يَلْبَسُونَ مِن سُندُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُّتَقَٰبِلِينَ <sup>54</sup>كَذَٰلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ <sup>55</sup>يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكُلِّ فَٰكِهَةٍ ءَامِنِينَ <sup>56</sup>لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلَّا ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَوَقَىٰهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ <sup>57</sup>فَضْلًا مِّن رَّبِّكَ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ <sup>58</sup>فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ <sup>59</sup>فَٱرْتَقِبْ إِنَّهُم مُّرْتَقِبُونَ
translation.text: <sup>40</sup>Assuredly the Day of Decision is the term for all of them, <sup>41</sup>A day when friend can in naught avail friend, nor can they be helped, <sup>42</sup>Save him on whom Allah hath mercy. Lo! He is the Mighty, the Merciful. <sup>43</sup>Lo! the tree of Zaqqum, <sup>44</sup>The food of the sinner! <sup>45</sup>Like molten brass, it seetheth in their bellies <sup>46</sup>As the seething of boiling water. <sup>47</sup>(And it will be said): Take him and drag him to the midst of hell, <sup>48</sup>Then pour upon his head the torment of boiling water. <sup>49</sup>(Saying): Taste! Lo! thou wast forsooth the mighty, the noble! <sup>50</sup>Lo! this is that whereof ye used to doubt. <sup>51</sup>Lo! those who kept their duty will be in a place secured. <sup>52</sup>Amid gardens and watersprings, <sup>53</sup>Attired in silk and silk embroidery, facing one another. <sup>54</sup>Even so (it will be). And We shall wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes. <sup>55</sup>They call therein for every fruit in safety. <sup>56</sup>They taste not death therein, save the first death. And He hath saved them from the doom of hell, <sup>57</sup>A bounty from thy Lord. That is the supreme triumph. <sup>58</sup>And We have made (this Scripture) easy in thy language only that they may heed. <sup>59</sup>Wait then (O Muhammad). Lo! they (too) are waiting.
